_about: Build projects (K-12). Science and engineering projects open a simulation from the School Library (PhET, CC BY 4.0) by its content id; robotics opens Reeborg's World; AI projects open Python Lab with starter code. Written by Umanah (AI agent, 2026-09-30). Bands: discover K-2, explore 3-5, build 6-8, launch 9-12.

science.title: Make Ten
science.question: How many different ways can you make 10?
steps: Open the game and choose the first level.
Make 10 by moving the blocks together.
Try to find a new way each time.
science.record: Write or draw two ways you made 10.

science.title: Mixing Light
science.question: What color do you see when red and green light mix?
steps: Turn on the red light and the green light.
Move the sliders and watch the person's thought bubble.
Try red and blue, then green and blue.
science.record: Which two lights made yellow? Which made purple?

science.title: Solids, Liquids and Gases
science.question: What happens to the tiny particles when you heat ice?
steps: Choose water and start as a solid.
Add heat slowly and watch the particles.
Stop when it boils and compare how fast the particles move.
science.record: Describe the particles in a solid, a liquid and a gas in one sentence each.

science.title: Will It Float?
science.question: Why do some blocks float and others sink?
steps: Predict which blocks will float before you drop them.
Drop each block in the water.
Check the mass and volume of each block.
science.record: Make a table: block, prediction, result. What do the floating blocks have in common?

science.title: Pushes and Pulls
science.question: What happens when two teams pull with the same force?
steps: Open Net Force.
Add pullers to each side and press Go.
Change one side and watch which way the cart moves.
science.record: Explain balanced and unbalanced forces with your own example.

science.title: Skate Park Energy
science.question: Where is the skater fastest, and why?
steps: Turn on the energy bar graph.
Drop the skater from different heights.
Watch kinetic and potential energy as the skater moves.
science.record: Sketch the track and mark where kinetic energy is highest and lowest.

science.title: Natural Selection
science.question: How does the environment change which bunnies survive?
steps: Add a mutation such as brown fur.
Add wolves, then change the environment.
Watch the population graph over several generations.
science.record: Write a claim, the evidence from the graph, and your reasoning.

science.title: Build an Atom
science.question: What decides which element an atom is?
steps: Add protons, neutrons and electrons.
Watch the element name and charge change.
Make a neutral carbon atom, then an ion.
science.record: What changes the element? What changes the charge? What changes the mass?

science.title: Gravity and Orbits
science.question: What would happen to Earth's orbit if the Sun were heavier?
steps: Start with the Sun and Earth.
Turn on the path and the gravity arrows.
Change the Sun's mass and compare the orbit.
science.record: Describe how mass changes the pull of gravity.

science.title: The Greenhouse Effect
science.question: How do greenhouse gases change a planet's temperature?
steps: Start with no greenhouse gases and read the temperature.
Add greenhouse gases in steps.
Record the temperature at each step.
science.record: Make a table of gas level and temperature. What pattern do you see?

science.title: Gene Expression
science.question: How does a cell make a protein from a gene?
steps: Place the positive regulator and RNA polymerase.
Watch messenger RNA form.
Bring the mRNA to the ribosome and collect proteins.
science.record: Explain transcription and translation in your own words.

science.title: Projectile Motion
science.question: Which launch angle sends a projectile farthest?
steps: Keep the speed the same.
Launch at 15, 30, 45, 60 and 75 degrees.
Measure each distance with the tape.
science.record: Graph angle against distance. Which angle wins, and why do pairs of angles match?

engineering.title: Balance the Plank
engineering.goal: Balance two different masses on a plank.
constraints: Use at least two different objects.
The plank must stay level when the supports are removed.
engineering.test: Remove the supports. Does it stay level?
engineering.improve: Find a rule that predicts where to put each mass.

engineering.title: Light the House
engineering.goal: Build a circuit that lights two bulbs with one switch.
constraints: Both bulbs must turn on and off with the same switch.
engineering.test: Close the switch: do both bulbs light? Open it: do both go out?
engineering.improve: Rebuild it so one bulb keeps working if the other breaks. What did you change?

engineering.title: Design a Spring Scale
engineering.goal: Use a spring to find the mass of an unknown object.
constraints: Use only the spring, the ruler and the known masses.
engineering.test: Measure the stretch for known masses, then predict the unknown mass.
engineering.improve: How could you make the scale more accurate?

engineering.title: Build a Boat That Floats
engineering.goal: Find which blocks can make a boat that carries the most weight.
constraints: The boat must float, not sink.
engineering.test: Compare how much each material floats in the water.
engineering.improve: Which material would you choose for a real boat, and why?

engineering.title: Safe Roller Coaster
engineering.goal: Design a track where the skater makes it over a hill and stops safely.
constraints: The skater must not fly off the track.
engineering.test: Run the skater five times. Does it work every time?
engineering.improve: Add friction. What changes, and how do you fix it?

engineering.title: Hit the Target
engineering.goal: Hit the target at 15 m on your first try.
constraints: Plan with the numbers before you launch.
engineering.test: Launch once. How close did you get?
engineering.improve: Change one thing at a time until you hit it, then explain your method.

robotics.title: Guide the Explorer
robotics.goal: Use blocks to guide the explorer through the maze.

robotics.title: Robot's First Steps
robotics.goal: Program the robot to walk home with move() and turn_left().

robotics.title: Around the World
robotics.goal: Make the robot walk around the world and come back.

robotics.title: Robot Hurdles
robotics.goal: Jump the hurdles and reach the finish.

robotics.title: Robot Sensors
robotics.goal: Hurdles move each time: make the robot sense them with front_is_clear().

robotics.title: Maze Solver
robotics.goal: Write one program that solves any maze by following the right-hand wall.

ai.title: Teach a Computer to Sort Fruit
ai.goal: See how an AI labels something new by finding the most similar example (nearest neighbour).

ai.title: Build a Spam Filter
ai.goal: Train a filter from word counts, then try to fool it.

ai.title: Predict Tomorrow's Temperature
ai.goal: Fit a line to data and see where predictions stop being trustworthy.

ai.title: Make a Rule-Based Chatbot
ai.goal: Build a chatbot from rules and compare it with a modern AI tutor.

ai.title: Pictures Are Numbers
ai.goal: See how a computer stores a picture, the first step of image recognition.
